{
  "decision": {
    "mode": "commands",
    "questions": [],
    "commands": [
      {
        "warnings": [],
        "risk": "low",
        "title": "Confirm the operating system",
        "explanation": "This only reads release information. Check that the installation actually reports Ubuntu 24.04 before selecting later update and hardening steps.",
        "requires_admin": false,
        "command": "cat /etc/os-release",
        "expected_result": "Distribution name and release details."
      },
      {
        "warnings": [],
        "risk": "low",
        "title": "Identify the running kernel",
        "explanation": "This reads the active kernel version. Later, compare it with installed updates to determine whether a maintenance restart is needed.",
        "requires_admin": false,
        "command": "uname -r",
        "expected_result": "The running kernel release."
      },
      {
        "warnings": [],
        "risk": "low",
        "title": "Check the current account's privileges",
        "explanation": "This lists your identity and group memberships without changing permissions. It helps distinguish ordinary access from administrative capability.",
        "requires_admin": false,
        "command": "id",
        "expected_result": "Your user ID, primary group, and supplementary groups."
      },
      {
        "warnings": [
          "Account inventories can contain personal names; avoid sharing them publicly."
        ],
        "risk": "low",
        "title": "Inventory accounts",
        "explanation": "This reads accounts through the configured identity providers. Review human accounts and login shells; do not assume unfamiliar service accounts are malicious.",
        "requires_admin": false,
        "command": "getent passwd",
        "expected_result": "Account records, home directories, and configured shells."
      },
      {
        "warnings": [],
        "risk": "low",
        "title": "Check filesystem capacity",
        "explanation": "This reads disk usage. Low space can prevent updates, backups, and security logs from working reliably.",
        "requires_admin": false,
        "command": "df -h",
        "expected_result": "Mounted filesystem sizes, usage, and available space."
      },
      {
        "warnings": [],
        "risk": "low",
        "title": "Inspect storage layout",
        "explanation": "This reads block-device and filesystem information. Encryption-related device layers may be visible, but this alone does not prove every sensitive volume is encrypted.",
        "requires_admin": false,
        "command": "lsblk -f",
        "expected_result": "Disks, partitions, filesystem types, and mount locations."
      },
      {
        "warnings": [],
        "risk": "low",
        "title": "Inventory network addresses",
        "explanation": "This reads interface addresses to establish the network context. Preserve the interface and address used for SSH when planning later access rules.",
        "requires_admin": false,
        "command": "ip -brief address",
        "expected_result": "Interfaces, link states, and IPv4 and IPv6 addresses."
      },
      {
        "warnings": [],
        "risk": "low",
        "title": "Inspect routing",
        "explanation": "This reads the IPv4 routing table. Routes help identify the active network path, but do not establish whether internet-side port forwarding exists.",
        "requires_admin": false,
        "command": "ip route show",
        "expected_result": "IPv4 routes and any default gateway."
      },
      {
        "warnings": [
          "If noninteractive sudo is unavailable, pause privileged checks rather than changing sudo policy."
        ],
        "risk": "low",
        "title": "Inventory listening services",
        "explanation": "This reads TCP and UDP listeners with process ownership where permitted. Note bindings on all interfaces and unexpected ports; a listener is not by itself proof of internet exposure.",
        "requires_admin": true,
        "command": "sudo -n ss -lntup",
        "expected_result": "Listening sockets, addresses, ports, and associated processes."
      },
      {
        "warnings": [],
        "risk": "low",
        "title": "Discover installed service units",
        "explanation": "This reads unit names and enablement states, including possible SSH socket activation. Use the observed exact names for later inspection rather than assuming how SSH starts.",
        "requires_admin": false,
        "command": "systemctl list-unit-files --no-pager",
        "expected_result": "Installed unit files and their enablement states."
      },
      {
        "warnings": [],
        "risk": "low",
        "title": "Inventory running services",
        "explanation": "This reads active services to compare with your intended uses. Keep unfamiliar services unchanged until their dependencies and purpose are understood.",
        "requires_admin": false,
        "command": "systemctl list-units --type=service --state=running --no-pager",
        "expected_result": "Currently running service units."
      },
      {
        "warnings": [],
        "risk": "low",
        "title": "Check failed units",
        "explanation": "This reads existing failures that could complicate hardening. Investigate failures affecting networking, authentication, storage, or logging before making changes.",
        "requires_admin": false,
        "command": "systemctl --failed --no-pager",
        "expected_result": "Failed units, or an indication that none are failed."
      },
      {
        "warnings": [
          "A missing executable means UFW is unavailable; an inactive UFW does not prove there are no other firewall rules."
        ],
        "risk": "low",
        "title": "Inspect UFW status",
        "explanation": "This reads UFW's state and any configured rules without enabling it. Compare both IPv4 and IPv6 allowances with required SSH access.",
        "requires_admin": true,
        "command": "sudo -n ufw status verbose",
        "expected_result": "Firewall status and rules, or an availability or privilege error."
      },
      {
        "warnings": [
          "Installed-package output can be lengthy; the app can capture it in numbered pages."
        ],
        "risk": "low",
        "title": "Inventory installed packages",
        "explanation": "This reads installed packages to identify SSH, update automation, security tools, and application stacks. It does not install, remove, or refresh anything.",
        "requires_admin": false,
        "command": "apt list --installed",
        "expected_result": "Installed package names and versions."
      },
      {
        "warnings": [
          "Cached package metadata may be stale, so this is not a complete assessment of outstanding security updates."
        ],
        "risk": "low",
        "title": "Inspect currently known upgrades",
        "explanation": "This reads upgrades known to the existing package cache. A later approved metadata refresh is needed before making patch decisions.",
        "requires_admin": false,
        "command": "apt list --upgradable",
        "expected_result": "Available upgrades according to locally cached metadata."
      },
      {
        "warnings": [],
        "risk": "low",
        "title": "Inspect scheduled maintenance",
        "explanation": "This reads timers to look for update and maintenance scheduling. A listed timer alone does not establish that security updates are configured correctly or succeeding.",
        "requires_admin": false,
        "command": "systemctl list-timers --all --no-pager",
        "expected_result": "Timers, their associated services, and scheduling information."
      },
      {
        "warnings": [
          "A missing aa-status executable requires later investigation, not immediate installation."
        ],
        "risk": "low",
        "title": "Inspect AppArmor enforcement",
        "explanation": "This reads the kernel application-confinement status. Distinguish enforced profiles from complain-mode profiles and unconfined applications.",
        "requires_admin": true,
        "command": "sudo -n aa-status",
        "expected_result": "AppArmor status and profile enforcement information."
      },
      {
        "warnings": [
          "Logs can contain usernames, network addresses, and application details."
        ],
        "risk": "low",
        "title": "Review recent warning and error logs",
        "explanation": "This reads at most 100 warning-or-higher journal entries from the last day. Look for authentication, update, storage, and security-control failures; this is not a complete intrusion assessment.",
        "requires_admin": true,
        "command": "sudo -n journalctl --since '24 hours ago' -p warning -n 100 --no-pager",
        "expected_result": "A bounded recent log sample, or no matching entries."
      }
    ]
  },
  "roadmap": [
    {
      "checks": [
        "Review the read-only results above before selecting any changes; unavailable tools and denied access are evidence gaps, not permission to install or reconfigure anything.",
        "Confirm which accounts, applications, shares, containers, and network services are essential, plus the SSH port, allowed clients, authentication method, and any router forwarding.",
        "Assess exposure to internet attackers, untrusted local-network peers, malicious applications, and physical theft separately.",
        "If credible compromise indicators appear, pause ordinary hardening and prioritize evidence preservation and recovery from a trusted environment."
      ],
      "purpose": "Establish the actual system state and access requirements without modifying it.",
      "title": "1. Discovery and threat model"
    },
    {
      "checks": [
        "Confirm the existing backups include essential data and configuration, and test restoring a representative file.",
        "Check that recovery media boots and that any disk-encryption recovery material is available offline.",
        "Before later edits, preserve original settings and permissions, document each change, and define a local-console restoration procedure.",
        "Retain the working console and an existing SSH session throughout access-related changes."
      ],
      "purpose": "Make failed changes recoverable before any hardening begins.",
      "title": "2. Recovery readiness and configuration baselines"
    },
    {
      "checks": [
        "After discovery, verify configured repositories and support coverage for the installed packages; identify third-party sources requiring separate maintenance.",
        "With approval, refresh package metadata and review proposed updates, free space, and application compatibility before installation.",
        "Apply supported security updates in a maintenance window; plan any restart separately with console and recovery access available.",
        "Verify package health, essential applications, SSH connectivity, and the running kernel afterward."
      ],
      "purpose": "Reduce exposure to known vulnerabilities using supported software.",
      "title": "3. Supported OS and patch baseline — awaits observations"
    },
    {
      "checks": [
        "Review human accounts, administrative groups, service identities, and stale access against the owner's actual needs.",
        "Inspect effective sudo policy before narrowing privileges; preserve a tested administrative recovery route.",
        "Review password policy, session locking, and account recovery without exposing password hashes or credentials.",
        "Stage any account restrictions individually and verify legitimate access before proceeding."
      ],
      "purpose": "Limit unnecessary authority while preserving legitimate administration.",
      "title": "4. Accounts and least privilege — awaits observations"
    },
    {
      "checks": [
        "Inspect the discovered SSH service or socket, included configuration files, effective settings, authorized keys, and relevant permissions.",
        "Confirm the exact SSH port and required client networks; assess IPv4, IPv6, and any router or cloud filtering.",
        "Back up settings, test a second independent SSH session, and validate proposed server configuration before any reload.",
        "Only tighten password or root authentication after an alternate administrative login is proven; evaluate MFA against recovery needs.",
        "If a test fails, keep the original session open and restore the saved configuration from the console before retrying."
      ],
      "purpose": "Strengthen remote authentication without losing required SSH access.",
      "title": "5. SSH and authentication — awaits observations"
    },
    {
      "checks": [
        "Map every listener to an essential purpose and inspect dependencies before proposing service restrictions.",
        "Determine which firewall manager already owns policy; avoid layering conflicting managers.",
        "Before enabling or tightening filtering, preserve SSH on its observed port and allow other confirmed essential traffic.",
        "Stage rules with console recovery available and a documented way to restore the previous policy.",
        "Verify new SSH sessions and intended application access from another device, including IPv6 where applicable; check that unwanted exposure is blocked."
      ],
      "purpose": "Minimize reachable attack surface while preserving required connectivity.",
      "title": "6. Exposed services and firewall — awaits observations"
    },
    {
      "checks": [
        "Inspect security-update automation configuration, logs, scheduling, and restart policy before modifying it.",
        "Verify logging persistence, retention, disk limits, time synchronization, and access restrictions.",
        "Select proportionate alerting for authentication failures, update failures, security-service failures, and resource exhaustion.",
        "Confirm alerts reach the owner and distinguish routine internet scanning from actionable events."
      ],
      "purpose": "Keep protection current and make important failures visible.",
      "title": "7. Automated updates, logging, and monitoring — awaits observations"
    },
    {
      "checks": [
        "Review sensitive application data, SSH material, backup destinations, and shared directories using their observed exact paths.",
        "Correct only demonstrated permission problems; avoid blanket or recursive ownership and permission changes.",
        "Review AppArmor coverage and test application behavior before strengthening profiles.",
        "Assess encryption, browser and application updates, container privileges, and secrets handling against the threat model.",
        "Preserve originals and restore narrowly if application functionality regresses."
      ],
      "purpose": "Protect data and contain application compromise without breaking workloads.",
      "title": "8. Applications and data protections — awaits observations"
    },
    {
      "checks": [
        "Repeat the relevant inventory checks and compare listeners, accounts, updates, firewall policy, and confinement with the baseline.",
        "Test essential applications and a fresh SSH login after each access-related change, not only at the end.",
        "Validate external exposure from an authorized second device; local status alone cannot establish internet reachability.",
        "Record approved changes, remaining risks, rollback procedures, and owners.",
        "Set recurring reviews for updates, accounts, exposed services, alerts, and restore tests; revisit the plan when services or networks change."
      ],
      "purpose": "Demonstrate that hardening works, preserve recoverability, and prevent configuration drift.",
      "title": "9. Verification and ongoing maintenance"
    }
  ],
  "explanation": "This is a planning-only proposal: nothing has run. The ordered commands perform read-only discovery; all configuration changes wait for observations and review. No configuration guarantees immunity, so the roadmap combines prevention, detection, verification, and recovery while explicitly preserving SSH access.",
  "assumptions": [
    "The supplied target is Ubuntu 24.04 LTS with bash, a local console, recovery media, backups, and required SSH access.",
    "Each command is separately reviewed and approved; sending command text does not press Enter.",
    "Privileged discovery uses noninteractive sudo only. If authorization is unavailable, leave that check unresolved rather than weakening privilege controls.",
    "Read-only commands do not intentionally alter configuration, although normal auditing or sudo logging may record their use.",
    "Essential services, SSH client networks, effective SSH settings, and backup recoverability remain unverified; they must be established before risky changes.",
    "Discovery output may contain identifying information and should be handled privately."
  ]
}
